Alex / team —

Thanks for the annotated SIG and the retention callout. A few technical clarifications and a concrete proposal for the MAP acceptance gate: 

1) Retention/archival model
- Redwood supports per-customer retention tiers. For 7-year archival we use a write-once S3-backed archival store with object immutability; we can provide a deletion/archival manifest and signed timestamped receipts upon request.
- If Commercia requires contractual proof of deletion, we can add an archival-verification deliverable and offer optional third-party attestation at an additional fee.

2) Residency mapping
- We will produce a Data Classification Annex that lists data classes (PII, transaction ledger, telemetry) and the allowed storage regions (US, EU). For regulated accounts requiring EU residency, we can commit to hosting in the EU region for those specific data classes on the MAP go-live date.

3) Objective MAP acceptance template (proposed to be checked off in Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.xlsx):
- SIG: Completed Worksheet uploaded to shared Drive; no "high" findings; all "medium" items have remediation owner and ETA within 60 days
- SOC2: Either Type II report within last 18 months OR bridge letter + evidence bundle uploaded to shared Drive and verified by Commercia InfoSec
- DPA: Fully executed DPA with Residence Annex or signed Risk Acceptance for non-EU hosting
- Staging test: Smoke test executed in target region with sample dataset and runbook executed without retention or access deviations

4) Timeline (suggested):
- 2026-10-26: SIG completed (Redwood intake -> Commercia review)
- 2026-10-28: DPA redline cycle closed (legal teams)
- 2026-11-05: SOC2 evidence bundle delivered
- 2026-11-09: Acceptance decision (pass/fail) and go/no-go for production rollout

If helpful I can draft the Data Classification Annex and the retention SLA language for the DPA. Also, note that third-party attestation (for deletion receipts) is typically a one-time professional services engagement.
